Catholic priests not like ‘fake bishops’, Atiku flays presidency’s attack on Onaiyekan
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Presidential Candidate of the African Democratic Congress ADC, Atiku Abubakar, has condemned the Presidency’s attack on the Catholic Church and John Cardinal Onaiyekan, accusing the President Bola Tinubu administration of growing intolerant of dissent and uncomfortable truths. In a statement by his Senior Special Assistant on Public Communication, Phrank Shaibu on Sunday, Atiku said the Presidency chose intimidation and political attacks instead of reflecting on the substance of the cleric’s message. Catholic bishops had recently had an engagement with the president, where the latter defended his record and the independence of the electoral umpire. However, the cardinal in a television interview on Friday said the Catholic bishops told the president that the country is bleeding and the economy is not helping poor citizens. According to him, Tinubu and his officials present at the meeting were “not looking very happy” with the speech, adding that it was a different speech from what the president usually listens to. But the president slammed Onaiyekan, accusing him and the Catholic Church, among other things, of working for the Nigeria Democratic Congress NDC presidential candidate, Mr Peter Obi. Atiku suggested the Presidency’s response reflected a habit of surrounding itself with fake and compliant clerics allegedly used in the lead up to the 2023 general election, contrasting this with the independence of Catholic bishops. “Perhaps the Presidency has become so accustomed to inviting ‘fake bishops’ that it now assumes every cleric can be recruited into political propaganda. But Catholic bishops are different. They are not political props, rented cheerleaders or praise singers. They are shepherds with a moral obligation to speak truth to power, regardless of whose interests are bruised. They cannot be used,” he said. The former Vice President said the Catholic Church has historically served as a moral voice for the poor and vulnerable regardless of who occupies Aso Rock, and praised the bishops for confronting President Tinubu directly. He described the Presidency’s commentary against Cardinal Onaiyekan as arrogant and unbecoming of government, accusing officials of attempting to distort the cleric’s engagement with the President. According to him, what the media managers of the Tinubu administration attempted to do was to cancel and overwrite the voices of the Catholic Bishops by selectively editing and reframing their engagement with the president in order to manufacture a narrative favourable to the government. He said Cardinal Onaiyekan’s decision to speak to the Press afterward was merely an effort to place the facts on record. “A government confident in its record welcomes criticism because it provides an opportunity for reflection and improvement. Only an insecure government wages war against honest voices while rewarding those who tell it only what it wants to hear,” he said. The former vice president noted that the Cardinal’s comments merely reflected the daily realities of hunger, insecurity, poverty, unemployment and the cost-of-living crisis confronting Nigerians, and that attacking him would not erase those realities. Atiku demanded that the Presidency apologises to the Catholic Church, Cardinal Onaiyekan and Catholic faithful nationwide, warning that the administration would continue to face accusations of arrogance and intolerance until it did so. The post Catholic priests not like ‘fake bishops’, Atiku flays presidency’s attack on Onaiyekan appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Thugs injure 10 PDP members in Ebonyi, as party seeks security probe
items.description: …PDP condemns attack on members, journalists; APC denies involvement By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki ABAKALIKI — At least 10 members of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) were injured after unidentified hoodlums attacked a political gathering in Ikwuator Idembia, Ezza South Local Government Area of Ebonyi State. The victims were reportedly receiving treatment in various hospitals following the incident, which occurred during a rally organised to welcome a former member of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Ifeanyi Nworie, into the PDP. According to eyewitnesses, the event was initially scheduled to hold at a village square but was disrupted by the attackers. The gathering was subsequently relocated to Nworie’s private residence, where the assailants allegedly followed and attacked participants. Witnesses said plastic chairs, canopies, a public address system and other property were damaged during the incident. It was also alleged that journalists travelling to cover the event were attacked on their way to the venue. Reacting to the incident, the Ebonyi State chapter of the PDP condemned the attacks on its members and journalists, describing them as a threat to democratic participation. Addressing journalists, the state Chairman of the party, Chukwuma Igwe, alleged that PDP members had faced repeated intimidation in recent weeks and called on security agencies to investigate the incident. He urged the Nigeria Police Force, the Department of State Services (DSS), the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), the Armed Forces and other security agencies to ensure the protection of all political parties and guarantee a level playing field ahead of the 2027 general elections. “We call on all security agencies to uphold their constitutional responsibility of protecting all Nigerians and ensuring that every citizen of Ebonyi State is free to exercise his or her civic and political rights,” Igwe said. He added that the PDP would not be intimidated and urged party members to remain peaceful and law-abiding. The PDP chairman also appealed to the Ebonyi State Government to uphold democratic principles, stressing that no individual or group has a monopoly on violence. Meanwhile, the APC denied any involvement in the attack. The Ebonyi State Chairman of the party, Chief Stanley Okoro Emegha, described the APC as a peaceful party and rejected allegations linking it to the incident. According to him, individuals dissatisfied with Nworie’s political decisions may have been responsible for the attack. “Our governor does not support violence, and APC members have been advised to conduct themselves peacefully,” Emegha said. He added that the party had no reason to sponsor violence and insisted that the APC was not connected with the incident. The attack also reportedly targeted journalists travelling in an official vehicle belonging to the Correspondents’ Chapel of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ). According to accounts from those affected, the assailants allegedly attempted to vandalise the vehicle and were prevented from causing further damage when the driver drove away from the scene. The journalists further alleged that one of the individuals at the scene warned them against returning to the community. The police had yet to issue an official statement on the incident as of the time of filing this report. The post Thugs injure 10 PDP members in Ebonyi, as party seeks security probe appeared first on Vanguard News .

Holcim to sell Philippines unit to China’s Huaxin in $807 million deal
items.description: Swiss building materials ‌supplier Holcim Group said on Sunday it plans to sell its Philippines business to China’s Huaxin Building Materials in a deal that could raise at least $807 million. Holcim will sell an initial 68% stake for $527 million with ​the remainder to be sold over the next three to five years for a ​minimum price of $280 million. This would lead to an overall valuation of $807 million, although ⁠the figure could rise “based on incremental value creation during this period,” Holcim said. The sale, which ​is expected to be completed in the first half of 2027, is Holcim’s biggest divestment since ​it sold its Nigeria business, also to Huaxin Cement, in a $1 billion deal in December 2024. Money raised from the sale of the Philippines business will be used to fund large acquisitions and also further investment in ​Holcim’s existing business. The Swiss company has been focusing more on Europe, Latin America, North Africa and ​Australia as it reshapes its business after spinning off its North American operations into a separate company last year. Acquisitions ‌have ⁠been identified as a key part of Holcim’s growth strategy, with the company planning to make around 15 deals in 2026. Holcim last year said it had 3 billion Swiss francs to 4 billion Swiss francs ($3.72 billion to $4.95 billion) to spend on acquisitions up to 2030, and could raise ​up to 6 billion ​Swiss francs more ⁠from divestments and extra borrowing for large deals and share buybacks. Holcim CEO Miljan Gutovic on Friday said the company had a “very healthy pipeline” of ​acquisition projects in Latin America, Europe and also parts of Asia, Middle ​East and ⁠Africa, and was also considering large deals. “We are constantly screening our landscape, from walling and flooring solution companies all the way to roofing, and we believe there are some very attractive markets,” he ⁠told analysts ​after the company’s second-quarter results . “I’m confident that we will have ​a strong momentum on the M&A front in the second half of this year,” Gutovic added.

items.title: Chinese military researchers tap US AI models to train defence systems
items.description: Chinese military researchers have used outputs from leading U.S. artificial intelligence models developed by OpenAI and Anthropic to ​train domestic AI systems to advance China’s defence capabilities, according to a Reuters review of more than 80 Chinese academic papers and patents. The previously unreported findings offer a rare glimpse into ‌how military and security-linked institutions in China are leveraging cutting-edge U.S. AI models as a shortcut to developing specialised systems of their own, despite Washington’s efforts to restrict Beijing’s access to advanced chips and other strategic technologies. The documents show widespread use of a technique known as “model distillation,” in which outputs from a powerful AI system are used to train smaller, specialised models that can be deployed locally without the enormous computing requirements needed to build frontier AI systems from scratch. Reuters’ review, which included compiled by the Washington-based Jamestown ​Foundation and shared exclusively with the news agency, showed distillation is widely used by researchers linked to the People’s Liberation Army and other military institutions. The papers suggest Chinese defence institutions see leading U.S. AI ​models as both a source of technical insight and a way to close the gap with American rivals. The documents show widespread use of a technique known as “model distillation,” in which outputs from a powerful AI system are used to train smaller, specialised models that can be deployed locally without the enormous computing requirements needed to build frontier AI systems from scratch. Reuters’ review, which included compiled by the Washington-based Jamestown ​Foundation and shared exclusively with the news agency, showed distillation is widely used by researchers linked to the People’s Liberation Army and other military institutions. The papers suggest Chinese defence institutions see leading U.S. AI ​models as both a source of technical insight and a way to close the gap with American rivals. The dispute centres on unauthorised extraction, not distillation itself, a widely ⁠used industry practice. The issue has emerged as a major flashpoint ahead of U.S.-China talks on AI governance and safety. U.S. officials have accused some Chinese entities of using distillation to extract capabilities from American AI models, potentially undermining export ​controls and infringing intellectual property rights. China has rejected the accusations, saying Washington is pursuing AI “hegemonism” while arguing that U.S. firms have engaged in similar practices. Chinese developers have also disputed claims that their AI advances rely on foreign models. AI startup Moonshot last ​week denied allegations by the Trump administration that its Kimi K3 model was built using distillation, saying it was driven by proprietary innovations. Sunny Cheung, a Jamestown fellow who analysed over 60 of the papers, said Chinese military scientists are systematically capturing the reasoning steps of Western models to adapt them for surveillance, cyber warfare and tactical decision-making. “Teaching a model the right answer is one thing but teaching it the reasoning behind the answer is much harder,” said Cheung. “These papers show Chinese military-linked researchers are trying to transfer that ​expensive, proprietary reasoning from Western models into smaller systems they can control and deploy locally.” Reuters verified the academic literature and identified an additional two dozen military-linked case studies. One paper published last year by researchers in PLA Unit 96941, a ​military intelligence and cyber-warfare unit in Beijing, described using OpenAI’s GPT-3.5 to process sensitive military source code. The researchers said third-party models were unsuitable for handling classified information. To overcome that limitation, they used GPT-3.5 to summarize software code and trained a ‌domestic model on ⁠those summaries to run entirely within Chinese military networks. The White House, Pentagon, China’s foreign ministry, the PLA and OpenAI did not respond to requests for comment. WIDE USE, FROM MONITORING TO MILITARY Chinese researchers have used distillation for purposes ranging from content monitoring to military deployment, Reuters’ and Jamestown’s review of the papers showed. At the North University of China, which has close links to the country’s weapons industry, researchers used Anthropic’s Claude 3 Haiku to generate synthetic training data for a text classification model for social media monitoring and content moderation. Anthropic said it does not provide commercial access to Claude in China or to Beijing-controlled firms and uses monitoring systems to detect policy violations. The company added that distilled models may ​lose the original systems’ safety safeguards, potentially allowing sensitive ​capabilities to be transferred to models beyond its ⁠control. A 2024 paper from the PLA’s National University of Defense Technology described using distillation to shrink an image-processing model for deployment on unmanned aerial vehicles, allowing drones to analyse live video and support navigation and targeting decisions in real time even when communications are cut. Similarly, researchers at China’s Academy of Military Sciences used distillation to run a ​target-recognition model on tactical hardware during simulated maritime operations involving drones, ships and unmanned submarines, a study published earlier this year showed. BENEFITS AND LIMITS China has embraced distillation ​as it seeks to compete ⁠with the U.S. in frontier AI while facing constraints on advanced computing resources due to Washington’s export controls on high-end chips. Central and local governments have promoted “model lightweighting” and edge computing, directing subsidies and research funding toward technologies that enable AI models to run on drones, satellites and other devices with limited processing power. Experts caution, however, that distillation has significant limitations. As Chinese AI models close the gap with their U.S. counterparts, military researchers are also examining distillation as a potential security ⁠risk. In January, researchers ​at the Army Engineering University published a paper on the threat of “data-free distillation,” a method of reverse-engineering a model’s capabilities without direct access ​to its core parameters. To counter that vulnerability, they proposed defense mechanisms designed to mask the hidden logical information exposed in a model’s public outputs. Distilled models also inherit only selected capabilities and cannot fully replicate the broad intelligence of frontier systems. Trevor Koverko, co-founder of AI data company Sapien, said ​distilled models remain less capable than their teacher models. “It is best understood as transferring selected capabilities into a cheaper, locally controlled system, not achieving independence from frontier AI.”

items.title: Pétrole : l’Algérie franchit le seuil de 1 million de barils/jour
items.description: La production algérienne de pétrole augmente en vertu d'une nouvelle décision prise au sein du groupe de concertation constitué de sept pays de l'OPEP+. L'Algérie voit sa production journalière de brut dépasser le million de barils pour la première fois depuis des années. L'annonce a été faite ce dimanche 2 août par le ministère des Hydrocarbures, à l’issue de la participation du ministre Mohamed Arkab aux réunions ministérielles consacrées au suivi de la mise en œuvre des mécanismes d’évaluation et de suivi des décisions des pays signataires de la déclaration de coopération (OPEP+). Les réunions se sont tenues en visioconférence et ont vu la participation, en plus du premier responsable du secteur, du PDG de Sonatrach , Noureddine Daoudi, et du président de l’Agence nationale de valorisation des ressources en hydrocarbures (ALNAFT), Abdelkader Cherafoui. Algérie : la production de pétrole augmente de 6.000 barils/jour La première rencontre était une réunion de coordination des sept pays engagés dans des réductions volontaires de production, avec la participation, outre celle du ministre algérien, des ministres du pétrole de l’Arabie saoudite, de l’Irak, du Kazakhstan, du Koweït, du Sultanat d’Oman et de la Russie. À l'issue des consultations, les sept pays ont décidé de procéder à une augmentation progressive de leur production collective de 188.000 barils par jour à compter de septembre 2026, dans le cadre de la suppression progressive des réductions volontaires de production adoptées à partir d'avril 2023, indique le ministère des Hydrocarbures. Conformément à cette décision, le niveau de production de l'Algérie augmentera de 6 000 barils par jour au cours du mois de septembre, pour atteindre 1,007 million de barils/jour, précise la même source. Les ministres ont réaffirmé leur engagement à poursuivre une “coordination étroite” et souligné l'importance d'un “suivi continu et attentif” de l'évolution du marché mondial du pétrole. Respect « strict » et « constant » des décisions du groupe de concertation Le ministre des Hydrocarbures a par la suite pris part aux travaux de la 67e réunion de la Commission ministérielle conjointe de suivi (JMMC), en présence des ministres des pays membres de la Commission (Algérie, Arabie saoudite, Irak, Koweït, Nigeria, Venezuela, Kazakhstan et Russie). Au cours de cette réunion, la commission a évalué le niveau d’engagement des pays signataires de la déclaration de coopération dans la mise en œuvre de leurs engagements relatifs aux réductions volontaires de production au cours des mois de mai et juin 2026. Les participants ont salué “les efforts continus” déployés par les pays participants, tout en soulignant que “le respect strict et constant des décisions collectives reste un facteur essentiel pour soutenir la stabilité du marché mondial du pétrole”. L’article Pétrole : l’Algérie franchit le seuil de 1 million de barils/jour est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Burkina / Éducation : Tenkodogo réunit les professeurs burkinabè autour du patriotisme, de la solidarité et des traditions
items.description: Burkina / Éducation : Tenkodogo réunit les professeurs burkinabè autour du patriotisme, de la solidarité et des traditions Tenkodogo, 31 juillet 2026 (AIB) – Le gouverneur de la région du Nakambé, Yiyé Abraham Somdo, a présidé jeudi au gouvernorat, la traditionnelle montée des couleurs nationales des corps constitués, avec la participation des membres de l'Amicale des professeurs du Burkina Faso (APB). Cette cérémonie a marqué top départ des activités de la 7e édition des « 72 heures de l'Amicale des professeurs du Burkina », qui se tient à Tenkodogo du 31 juillet au 2 août 2026, sous le thème de la fraternité, du patriotisme et de la solidarité. Selon le président de l'Amicale, Émile Lallsaga, l'APB est née d'un groupe d'échanges entre enseignants sur les réseaux sociaux avant d'être formalisée en 2022. Depuis, elle organise chaque année des retrouvailles pour renforcer les liens entre professeurs, promouvoir le tourisme intérieur et favoriser le partage d'expériences professionnelles. Présidant la montée des couleurs, le gouverneur Yiyé Abraham Somdo a salué une initiative qui transcende le cadre corporatiste pour contribuer à la cohésion sociale et au développement national. Il a invité les professeurs à poursuivre leur mission de transmission du savoir et des valeurs civiques, soulignant que dans le contexte actuel, l'éducation constitue un levier essentiel de consolidation de la souveraineté nationale. Après la cérémonie officielle, les participants ont rendu une visite de courtoisie à Sa Majesté Naaba Guiguempolé, Dima de Zoungrantenga. Une démarche par laquelle les enseignants ont témoigné leur respect aux autorités coutumières et réaffirmé leur attachement aux valeurs culturelles et traditionnelles du Burkina Faso. Dans l'après-midi, l'Amicale a traduit son engagement social par un don de kits de layette d'une valeur de 444 000 F CFA à une structure sanitaire de la localité, au profit des nouveau-nés et de leurs mères. Par cette 7e édition organisée dans le Nakambé, l'Amicale des professeurs du Burkina Faso entend promouvoir la fraternité, l'entraide et le civisme, tout en valorisant le patrimoine culturel et humain de la région hôte. Les activités se poursuivront par des panels d'échanges, des visites touristiques et des actions de solidarité. Agence d'Information du Burkina SM/ata

items.description: El último balance oficial eleva a 72 el número de migrantes muertos, según ha dado a conocer este domingo el delegado del Gobierno de Ceuta, Miguel Ángel Pérez Triano. Pese a este balance, las autoridades ceutíes sitúan en 88 los cadáveres recuperados del agua que ya han sido trasladados a su morgue. Algunos presentan un mayor deterioro debido a que los cuerpos siguen llegando a la costa ceutí más de dos semanas después. Ceuta intenta recuperar la normalidad después de la entrada irregular el pasado jueves de más de 50.000 personas desde Marruecos y, aunque la mayoría de ellas ha vuelto a su país, las Fuerzas de Seguridad y el Ejército realizan controles en las calles para conseguir que todas abandonen la ciudad. El paso de Beni-Enzar, único operativo en Melilla, cumple 24 horas desde su reapertura tras un cierre de día y medio por la crisis migratoria que ha obligado a reforzar las dotaciones de la Guardia Civil y la Policía Nacional para que la frontera con Marruecos vuelva a la normalidad. Tras un intento de entrada, los militares han ralentizado el tránsito. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Second phase of AJK polls conclude amid renewed rigging allegations by PPP
items.description: The second phase of the Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) elections took place on Sunday, with polling held in eight out of the nine constituencies of Muzaffarabad division and all 12 refugee constituencies. Polling began at 8am and continued till 5pm for the refugee seats, while the process concluded at 6pm in Muzaffarabad after an hour-long extension. The electoral process in LA-27 (Muzaffarabad-I) was postponed due to heavy rain, AJK Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Ghulam Mustafa Mughal said, DawnNewsTV reported . Over 300 candidates were in the fray for the Muzaffarabad seats and the 12 seats for refugees settled in different regions. What has happened so far: Polling suspended in LA-27 due to rain; 4 other seats up for grabs in Muzaffarabad district, 2 each in Neelum and Jhelum Valley Voting underway across country for 12 refugee seats — 7 in Punjab, other 5 divided between different provinces Bilawal condemns ‘attack’ on party’s regional president, says PPP worker died in LA-31 PPP alleges electoral malpractices at some polling stations in at least 11 constituencies Continuing his rigging allegations, PPP Chairperson Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Sunday accused the PML-N of “robbing” votes in the second phase of the AJK elections as well. In a post on X later in the day, he condemned an “attack” on party’s regional president Chaudhry Latif Akbar — also the candidate for LA-31 (Muzaffarabad-V). Accusing “miscreant elements of the PML-N” of being behind the incident, Bilawal said PPP worker Mushtaq Shah was killed in the same constituency. “The PML-N is robbing the votes of the people of Azad Kashmir through bullets, batons and coercion,” he alleged. The PPP chairman demanded that those responsible for the attack on Akbar and the “murderers” of the party worker be arrested immediately. In a separate statement , Bilawal said, “The PML-N has crossed all limits. Attacks are taking place on our voters and the president of the state (AJK).” He remarked that in Muzaffarabad, the PPP’s “politics of dignity and principles was in contest with the PML-N’s threat, rigging and coercion”. The PPP shared a complaint written to the Election Commission regarding a “physical assault” on Akbar. The party said the LA-31 candidate was “engaged in the electoral process on polling day” when the alleged incident took place, accusing three individuals. It said a first information report (FIR) was being registered and urged the Election Commission to order an inquiry into the “security lapse” that resulted in the incident. AJK Prime Minister Faisal Mumtaz Rathore, who belongs to the PPP, took notice of the incident and ordered the chief secretary and the police chief to take those responsible to justice. The AJK PM termed the attack “a slap on the politics of dignity and principle in Kashmir”. Akbar also wrote two letters to the Election Commission. In one, he alleged that an attempt on his life was made at Polling Station 177 “by PML-N workers” and wrote of the PPP worker’s death. He further claimed that his polling agents were not allowed to “sit in the polling area” at 14 polling stations. In the second letter, Akbar said PPP leader Syed Mumtaz Hussain Naqvi sustained bullet wounds in a “[murderous] attack” at a polling station in a building. Addressing a press conference, PPP leader Nayyar Hussain Bokhari claimed that eight party workers had been injured in the ongoing elections so far. Bokhari contended there was a “state of lawlessness” in AJK. Polls in AJK are being held in three phases over security concerns, with the first set of polls held in Mirpur division on July 27, the second held today, and the third phase set for August 10 across Poonch division. Ahead of today’s elections, internet services were restored in parts of Muzaffarabad division after remaining suspended for 54 days on July 29. At the time, it was not clear whether the restoration covered the entire division or was limited to the state capital. Addressing the media on Sunday, the AJK CEC said that a letter had been written yesterday to request the restoration of internet services. He added that the outcome would be known today, without providing further details. “We will work according to the law; we will not come under pressure from anyone,” CEC Mughal said while answering a question. PML-N says man did not die from bullet, had heart failure On its part, the PML-N disputed the PPP’s stance on the party worker’s death in Muzaffarabad, saying that he died due to a heart failure and did not suffer any bullet injury. Responding to the PPP’s stream of allegations in a media talk in Rawalpindi, PML-N Punjab Senior Minister Marriyum Aurangzeb said a man aged between 68 and 70 years was trying to resolve a “scuffle” when he suffered heart failure. She noted that there was a physical altercation between groups of the PML-N and the PPP, describing the incident as “unfortunate”. She further said that Shah’s family has refused to have a post-mortem examination conducted. “My brothers, this politics of bullet, this politics of robbing votes, this does not suit parties like us,” Aurangzeb said. She recalled the Charter of Democracy signed between the PPP and the PML-N in 2007, stressing that its purpose was not to let democratic processes be sabotaged. Noting that the PPP was in power in AJK and had its administrative machinery in the region, the PML-N leader questioned if Bilawal’s “own government is carrying out rigging against you”. She remarked that if one considered the PPP’s allegations to be true, the party would have to “accept” that its own government “carried out rigging against Bilawal”. Aurangzeb said the PPP-led administration was preventing the transportation of the required electoral equipment. She also commented on Bokhari showing ballot papers stamped with votes for PML-N, saying, “This is an election of thousands of votes. He was showing two stamps on two ballot papers.” The Punjab minister took aim at the PPP’s governance, saying that it had nothing to show for its performance. She quipped that voters were yet to head to polling stations early in the morning while the PPP had already started holding media talks on rigging. PPP alleges electoral malpractices On Sunday, the PPP alleged electoral malpractices shortly after polling commenced, with several of the complaints claiming its polling agents at some stations were not allowed to observe the voting process. At 2pm, the party also wrote a separate letter to the Election Commission requesting follow-up on 25 complaints filed by it regarding 11 constituencies. The PPP said it had not received any formal written response or acknowledgement from the electoral watchdog on the status of any of the 25 complaints. “Given the gravity, number and geographical spread of the violations documented, the Party respectfully submits that a formal response from the Commission is now overdue and urgently required.” On the other hand, the PML-N’s social media posts revolved around voters across Muzaffarabad and Punjab showing up to cast ballots with “ enthusiasm ”. Several posts highlighted that a large number of voters were flocking to its election camps with those of other parties PML-N’s election camps with election camps of the PPP. The PML-N also wrote to the Election Commission in response to a PPP complaint about LA-40 (Valley-I), terming the latter’s allegations against its candidate Muhammad Naeem Khan as “baseless”. In the letter, seen by Dawn , the PML-N asserted that the allegations “regarding administrative failures are unsubstantiated and appear to be an attempt to create unnecessary controversy around the polling process”. The PML-N urged the electoral watchdog to ensure that “no misleading or politically motivated complaint is allowed to undermine public confidence in the integrity of the polling”. ‘Ballot stuffing’ At a polling station in LA-32 (Muzaffarabad-VI), the PPP accused PML-N supporters of “ballot stuffing”. It further said that a government employee had been deployed as a polling agent for the PML-N at a separate polling station. In LA-30 (Muzaffarabad-IV), the PPP claimed PML-N workers removed a ballot box at the Banaw Langah polling station and placed it outside, where they were allegedly “stamping ballot papers”. In Charakhpora Union Council of LA-31 (Muzaffarabad-V), the PPP said “bogus voting” was taking place at the Sharik Kamal Bandi-Khalsa polling station. The party said the alleged act “directly subverts the integrity of the poll”, adding that the polling station also did not have adequate security despite being declared “sensitive”. The PPP also alleged a PML-N MPA at a polling station in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Abbottabad of obstructing the voting process for the refugee seat of LA-45 (Kashmir-VI). In LA-25 (Neelum-I), the PPP said the voting process at a polling station had been halted after reports emerged of PML-N supporters tearing up ballot papers. The PPP also said its polling agents at a polling station in LA-25’s Khawaja Sari reported that “fraudulent votes are being cast” there. It urged the Election Commission to dispatch officials and law enforcement to halt the alleged action. ‘Polling agents excluded’ The party alleged that its polling agents were not allowed to sit at polling stations for refugee seat LA-34 (Jammu-I) in Cantonment and Lahore’s Sheranwala Gate, calling on the Election Commission to intervene. The PPP wrote to the electoral watchdog about a similar complaint emerging from a polling station in Janabad, Sargodha, for LA-34. Sharing another letter addressed to the Election Commission about LA-34, the PPP said “elected members” of the PML-N were present inside a Pakpattan polling station and “stamping ballot papers”. It further claimed that its polling agent was “barred from entering the same polling station”. “The deliberate exclusion of the PPP’s oversight representative while PML-N’s own elected officials conduct fraud inside the station is not a coincidence — it is a coordinated strategy to commit electoral fraud without any independent witness,” it alleged. The party urged the electoral watchdog to dispatch law enforcement to the polling station and remove the PML-N supporters allegedly involved in “ballot stuffing”. Regarding LA-42 (Valley-III), the PPP filed a complaint over party candidate Asim Sharif Butt’s polling agent being “physically prevented” from entering a polling station in Muzaffargarh’s Alipur Tehsil. The PPP also claimed its polling agents at three polling stations in LA-30 (Muzaffarabad-IV) were denied from observing the electoral process. Similarly, the party said polling agents of candidate Ishfaq Zaffar were not permitted to take their seats at three polling stations in LA-32 (Muzaffarabad-VI). Terming it a “serious violation” of the electoral code of conduct, the PPP sought disciplinary action against the presiding officers who allegedly refused the agents from discharging their duties. At one of those polling stations, the PPP claimed a “violent confrontation” was underway between supporters of PML-N candidate Raja Farooq Haider and PPP supporters. Other issues In a separate statement in the morning, the party claimed that no polling staff was present at any of the 196 polling stations in LA-27, adding that this raised the concern that there was a “deliberate” attempt to delay the polling. Similarly, the party alleged that polling staff had reached late at 71 polling stations of LA-28, due to which the voting process was facing delays. The PPP claimed that a similar situation was being witnessed at several polling stations of LA-30, where polling staff had not arrived on time. Regarding LA-31, the PPP said it had written to the Election Commission on behalf of its candidate Akbar, urging it to take action over difficulties faced by voters due to the closure of the Rangla-Katkair Road in Muzaffarabad. The party said over 50 vehicles carrying voters were stuck due to the road’s closure. PML-N slams ‘blame game’ Earlier in the day, PML-N leader and Kashmir Affairs Minister Amir Muqam called on political parties not to indulge in a “blame game”. “Nothing is to be gained from a blame game,” he said during a press conference in Islamabad, adding that law enforcement personnel were also deployed to ensure security. “They should not act in a manner that ‘why was I not given seats’,” Muqam said, stressing that it was the public whose votes allocate seats. The minister urged all political parties to let the electoral process take place in a peaceful manner, stressing that making allegations without evidence cannot change the results. At the same time, Muqam also highlighted “arbitrary transfers and administrative decisions” in AJK, where the PPP is in power. He said the moves “seemed discriminatory”. He recalled that the PML-N had accepted the results of elections in Gilgit-Baltistan held in June, where the PPP emerged the winner and formed the government. Defending the results from Mirpur, Muqam asserted that the people voted for PML-N due to its performance. On the other hand, PPP leader Nadeem Afzal Chan also held a press conference where he called on the Election Commission to play its role in “proving” the election process in AJK to be free and fair. “Azad Kashmir is an international issue … people’s eyes are on it,” the former MNA said, adding that if the commission did not recognise the public and assure a free election, “tomorrow we will not be able to ratify this election under any circumstance”. He recalled that after the Mirpur polls, there was a detailed discussion within the party about boycotting the second and third phases. However, the party leadership refused the idea of a boycott. Chan cautioned that if the PPP was “compelled” to move towards such steps for the third phase, it would benefit those who wanted to prove the election “dirty”. “I see this becoming an ultra Form-47 election,” he said. He said that in negotiations in Muzaffarabad, the PPP had provided proof of rigging in four constituencies, as well as agreeing to hold re-polling in any other constituencies in which there were objections. He also called for a benchmark for voting, saying, “General polling was less than 30 per cent. But wherever you won, it was 80pc, 90pc, 75pc … this doesn’t even happen in urban cities like Islamabad and Lahore.” ‘Admission of rigging’ The PPP and the PML-N — coalition partners in the Centre — have been engaged in a war of words since the PML-N emerged in the lead during the first phase of polls. The PPP has accused the PML-N of rigging in Mirpur and demanded re-polling. Scuffles, violence and allegations of rigging had marred the polls in Mirpur, with the PML-N and PPP accusing each other of electoral malpractice. To defuse the tensions, senior leaders of both parties met multiple times in Azad Kashmir over the weekend to “explore a legal resolution” to the dispute. The latest round of talks followed two earlier meetings on Thursday and Friday. A PML-N source told Dawn that discussions focused on the PPP’s allegations and its demand for re-polling in certain constituencies. “It was not planned or pre-planned rigging but isolated acts at places where supporters of one candidate enjoyed numerical dominance over their opponents. Such incidents have unfortunately been part of the territory’s polling atmosphere and have also been witnessed in previous elections,” the source quoted the PML-N leaders as telling their counterparts. Referring to this statement in a X post on Sunday, Bilawal said: “Despite this admission from the rigging party, the [EC] has still failed to take action on our complaints from phase 1. Had they done so, the credibility of today’s phase 2 election would have been restored. “The PPP reserves the right to protest and demand re-election in phases where rigging took place, and the election commission failed to act. We have already sent multiple written complaints about ballot stuffing and illegal removal of our polling agents in today’s election. It is hoped the election commission acts swiftly and at least maintains fairness in round 2.” According to the sources, during meetings with the PML-N, PPP initially raised objections to the results in four constituencies — Charhoi, Sehnsa and Nakyal in Kotli district, and Barnala in Bhimber district during phase-I of the election. However, it later withdrew its allegations regarding Sehnsa and Barnala. Saturday’s discussions centred on Charhoi, where PPP AJK President Chaudhry Yasin lost to PML-N’s Raja Riasat, and Nakyal, where PPP candidate Javed Iqbal Budhanvi was defeated by PML-N’s Raja Ayaz Ahmed. Meanwhile, the Sharif family also held discussions at Jati Umra. According to a statement issued by the PM’s Office, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif held consultations with his elder brother and PML-N chief Nawaz Sharif at Jati Umra to take stock of mounting political challenges, including the rift with the PPP over the AJK elections. A senior PML-N leader told Dawn that the party leadership had taken serious note of the PPP chairman’s increasingly combative rhetoric against the Sharif family over the AJK polls and his warning that the PPP could reconsider its support for the federal government if the remaining phases of the elections were manipulated in favour of the PML-N. Election numbers According to the AJK Election Commission, 207 candidates are in the fray for the nine constituencies in Muzaffarabad division, comprising five seats in Muzaffarabad district and two each in Neelum and Jhelum Valley districts. Another 137 candidates are contesting the 12 refugee constituencies, including six seats representing refugees from the Kashmir Valley and six from Jammu. A total of 809,621 voters are registered in Muzaffarabad division, while the 12 refugee constituencies have a combined electorate of 438,834. According to the commission, 1,483 polling stations have been established across Muzaffarabad division, of which 533 have been declared highly sensitive, 741 sensitive and 209 normal. Another 1,057 polling stations have been set up for the 12 refugee constituencies. Out of 12 refugee seats, seven seats are in Punjab, one seat is in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, one seat (Jammu-VI) is divided between Pun­jab, Islamabad and KP, one seat is divided between Sindh and Balo­chistan (Valley-I), and one seat (Jammu-I) is shared among refugees living in Balochistan, Punjab and Sindh. Valley-V seat is divided between Punjab and Islamabad. In Rawalpindi and Islamabad, about 27,000 registered male and female voters will elect lawmakers for LA-43 (Valley-IV), LA-44 (Valley-V), and LA-39 (Jammu-VI) seats. A total of 175 polling stations have been established, out of which 18 polling stations in Rawalpindi have been declared sensitive. A total of 34 candidates are in the fray. In Gujrat, almost 2,000 policemen will perform security duties at scores of polling stations for the LA-38 elections . The total number of polling stations in these districts is 115, with 75 in Gujrat, 24 in Wazirabad and 16 in Mandi Bahauddin. The total number of voters is 50,225 in the entire constituency. As many as 11 candidates are contesting this seat. In Sindh, officials said the elections will be conducted on LA-34 (Jammu-I) and LA-40 (Kashmir Valley-I) with polling stations established across Karachi and other districts of Sindh. In LA-34 (Jammu-I), a total of 17 candidates are contesting the election, which has 698 registered voters in Karachi’s seven districts and 477 voters in 13 other districts of Sindh. For LA-40 Kashmir (Valley-I), 11 candidates are in the race. The constituency has 4,200 registered voters in Karachi and 403 voters in 17 other districts of Sindh. In Balochistan, seven polling booths have been established across the province for the Kashmir Valley-I constituency, where 1,174 registered voters are expected to cast their ballots. Balochistan shares this seat with Sindh. For the Jammu-I constituency, six polling booths have been set up, with a total of 182 registered voters, including 85 men and 97 women, eligible to vote. Polling stations have been established for AJK refugee voters residing in Balochistan at various locations, including Quetta, Pishin, Qila Saifullah, Hub, Loralai, Sibi, Mastung, Zhob and Barkhan. In KP, 41 polling stations, mostly in Swat and Mansehra, have been set up for the LA-45 (Kashmir VI) seat. Additional input from Ameer Hamza and Mohammad Asghar

items.title: Ijaw Elders dissociate from INC leadership, pledge intervention in crisis
items.description: By Adesina Wahab The Ijaw Elders Forum (IEF) has distanced itself from the current leadership and global structure of the Ijaw National Congress (INC), alleging constitutional breaches and a breakdown of internal democratic processes within the organisation. In a statement signed by its Chairman, Chief Bukazi Etete, and Secretary, Mr. Efiye Bribena, the forum expressed concern over what it described as the INC leadership’s failure to operate in accordance with the organisation’s constitution. According to the IEF, no institution can legitimately claim to represent the Ijaw people while failing to adhere to the constitutional framework from which it derives its authority. The forum further alleged that public confidence in the INC’s ability to protect the political, economic and environmental interests of the Ijaw people had diminished. As a result, the IEF said it would resume the advocacy role it played between 2015 and 2021, when it said internal disputes within the INC affected the organisation’s operations. The statement read in part: “Until all constitutional issues affecting the status, governance and legitimacy of the INC are conclusively resolved and constitutional order is restored, the Ijaw Elders Forum shall fill the resulting vacuum in advancing the collective interests of the Ijaw people, as it did between 2015 and 2021.” The forum said its intervention was intended as a temporary measure aimed at promoting the interests of the Ijaw nation until the leadership issues within the INC are resolved. It added that its objectives include promoting transparency and accountability in Ijaw advocacy, safeguarding the constitutional, political and resource rights of the Ijaw people, fostering regional unity, and engaging constructively with governments and other stakeholders in the Niger Delta. The IEF also called on traditional rulers, youth organisations, women’s groups, professionals and other stakeholders across the Niger Delta to support what it described as efforts to restore constitutional governance and institutional integrity within the Ijaw socio-cultural body. The leadership of the Ijaw National Congress had not responded to the forum’s claims as of the time of filing this report. The post Ijaw Elders dissociate from INC leadership, pledge intervention in crisis appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Contre l’oubli : la RDC commémore ses morts et œuvre à faire reconnaître le «génocide économique au Congo» à l’international
items.description: La Republique democratique du Congo honore ce 2 août les dizaines de millions de morts et de victimes des guerres et des conflits armes qui ont et continuent d'endeuiller le pays depuis pres de trois decennies. Cette commemoration est organisee dans le cadre de la Journee nationale du GENOCOST. Le terme est compose de la contraction de « Geno », referant au terme genocide, et de « Cost » signifiant coût en anglais. L'appellation GENOCOST designe le genocide que les Congolais ont subi a cause de l'exploitation economique de leurs richesses naturelles. Cette commemoration avait ete adoptee par l'Assemblee nationale congolaise et le Senat, avant d'etre promulguee par le president du pays, Felix Tshisekedi, le 26 decembre 2022. Le texte adopte fixe les principes fondamentaux relatifs a la protection et a la reparation des victimes. Il prevoit egalement une mobilisation nationale et internationale afin de marquer cette journee dans toutes les provinces ainsi qu'au sein des ambassades de la RDC, en reunissant citoyens et partenaires autour d'espaces de dialogue, de memoire et de paix. Bataille diplomatique pour faire reconnaître le GENOCOST a l'international Le gouvernement congolais s'est engage a faire reconnaître le « genocide economique au Congo » a une echelle internationale. Cette cause a deja ete portee a Geneve en 2025, lors de la 60ᵉ session du Conseil des droits de l'homme des Nations unies et plus recemment, en marge de l'Assemblee generale de l'ONU a New York, entre autres evenements dedies a la reconnaissance du genocide congolais. Les autorites du pays ont fait part de leurs efforts pour intensifier ce genre d'initiatives cette annee a l'occasion des grands forums mondiaux. Le texte de 2022 prevoit egalement la creation de deux institutions : le Fonds national de reparation des victimes de violences sexuelles (FONAREV) et la Commission interministerielle d'aide aux victimes et d'appui aux reformes (CIA-VAR), qui seront epaulees par l'expertise d'un nouveau Conseil consultatif international, mis en place afin d'examiner et de contribuer a la reconnaissance des atrocites commises en RDC trois decennies durant. Cet organe, compose de personnalites de premier plan issues des domaines du droit international, de la diplomatie et du monde universitaire, est copreside par la defenseuse congolaise des droits humains Julienne Lusenge et par Sir Howard Morrison KC, l'un des plus grands specialistes britanniques du droit penal international et du droit international humanitaire. En se basant sur les conclusions du rapport Mapping des Nations unies de 2010 et sur les violations recentes des droits de l'homme durant le conflit qui se poursuit toujours dans l'est de la RDC, le Conseil apportera son expertise sur les processus juridiques et diplomatiques necessaires a la reconnaissance officielle des atrocites perpetrees et a l'etablissement des responsabilites de leurs auteurs.

items.title: Burkina / Éducation : Tenkodogo réunit les professeurs burkinabè autour du patriotisme, de la solidarité et des traditions
items.description: Burkina / Éducation : Tenkodogo réunit les professeurs burkinabè autour du patriotisme, de la solidarité et des traditions Tenkodogo, 31 juillet 2026 (AIB) – Le gouverneur de la région du Nakambé, Yiyé Abraham Somdo, a présidé jeudi au gouvernorat, la traditionnelle montée des couleurs nationales des corps constitués, avec la participation des membres de l'Amicale des professeurs du Burkina Faso (APB). Cette cérémonie a marqué top départ des activités de la 7e édition des « 72 heures de l'Amicale des professeurs du Burkina », qui se tient à Tenkodogo du 31 juillet au 2 août 2026, sous le thème de la fraternité, du patriotisme et de la solidarité. Selon le président de l'Amicale, Émile Lallsaga, l'APB est née d'un groupe d'échanges entre enseignants sur les réseaux sociaux avant d'être formalisée en 2022. Depuis, elle organise chaque année des retrouvailles pour renforcer les liens entre professeurs, promouvoir le tourisme intérieur et favoriser le partage d'expériences professionnelles. Présidant la montée des couleurs, le gouverneur Yiyé Abraham Somdo a salué une initiative qui transcende le cadre corporatiste pour contribuer à la cohésion sociale et au développement national. Il a invité les professeurs à poursuivre leur mission de transmission du savoir et des valeurs civiques, soulignant que dans le contexte actuel, l'éducation constitue un levier essentiel de consolidation de la souveraineté nationale. Après la cérémonie officielle, les participants ont rendu une visite de courtoisie à Sa Majesté Naaba Guiguempolé, Dima de Zoungrantenga. Une démarche par laquelle les enseignants ont témoigné leur respect aux autorités coutumières et réaffirmé leur attachement aux valeurs culturelles et traditionnelles du Burkina Faso. Dans l'après-midi, l'Amicale a traduit son engagement social par un don de kits de layette d'une valeur de 444 000 F CFA à une structure sanitaire de la localité, au profit des nouveau-nés et de leurs mères. Par cette 7e édition organisée dans le Nakambé, l'Amicale des professeurs du Burkina Faso entend promouvoir la fraternité, l'entraide et le civisme, tout en valorisant le patrimoine culturel et humain de la région hôte. Les activités se poursuivront par des panels d'échanges, des visites touristiques et des actions de solidarité. Agence d'Information du Burkina SM/ata

items.title: Troops rescue 34 kidnap victims, arrest ISWAP informant, recover arms
items.description: Troops of the Nigerian Army have, in the last 24 hours, rescued 34 kidnap victims, apprehended suspected ISWAP informants and recovered arms and ammunition in coordinated operations nationwide. This is contained in an operational report made available to the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Sunday. The report said that troops of Operation HADIN KAI rescued 31 kidnap victims from terrorists along the Buratai-Kamuya road in Biu Local Government Area of Borno. It said the rescue followed a swift response after troops of 135 Special Forces Battalion detected ISWAP/JAS terrorists abducting civilians from four vehicles through CCTV surveillance. According to the report, troops immediately deployed a quick reaction force, engaged the terrorists and forced them to abandon the victims and flee, with one motorcycle left behind. “In another operation, troops of 145 Battalion conducted a fighting patrol to the Turoh general area of Damasak in Mobbar Local Government Area. “The terrorists reportedly fled on sighting the troops, leaving behind two motorcycles and illicit drugs recovered during exploitation of the area. “Also, troops of 232 Battalion Tactical apprehended a suspected ISWAP informant at Garaha Market in Hong Local Government Area of Adamawa,” it said. In the North-West, the report revealed that troops of Operation FANSAN YAMMA engaged terrorists moving with rustled cattle in Tsafe Local Government Area of Zamfara. It added that the troops’ superior firepower forced the terrorists to withdraw in disarray during the encounter. The report also revealed that troops of Operation MESA rescued a kidnapped woman and her two children along the old Obajana-Jakura-Tajimi road in Lokoja Local Government Area of Kogi. According to the report, preliminary investigation revealed that the victims were abducted on July 29 from a Ruga settlement in the Gada-Biyu area of the same local government. “In Plateau State, troops of Operation Enduring Peace responded to reports of an attack on a herder in Bassa Local Government Area. “The assailants had fled before the troops arrived, while the deceased and recovered cattle were handed over to the victim’s family,” it added. In the South-East, the report said the troops of Operation UDO KA recorded a major breakthrough with the arrest of three suspected terrorists linked to the ambush of troops in Imo on May 4. It added that the operation, conducted in Delta and Imo states, followed intelligence obtained from earlier arrested suspects. According to the report, troops recovered four AK-47 rifles, one FN rifle, a pistol, 11 AK-47 magazines, two FN magazines, 239 rounds of assorted ammunition, a fragmentation jacket and other military items from terrorist camps. “The recovered weapons included rifles earlier carted away during the May ambush on troops, while further exploitation led to the discovery of another terrorist camp containing additional arms and ammunition,” it said. The post Troops rescue 34 kidnap victims, arrest ISWAP informant, recover arms appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Oil Resumption: Dialogue best path forward, MOSOP tells Ogonis
items.description: …Urges speedy completion of FG’s peace process …Commends Tinubu, Ribadu for dialogue initiative By Daniel Abia PORT HARCOURT — The Movement for the Survival of the Ogoni People (MOSOP) has urged Ogoni communities to embrace dialogue as the Federal Government advances efforts to resolve longstanding issues surrounding the resumption of oil exploration in Ogoniland after 36 years. Speaking at the Ogoni National Rally in Gokana Local Government Area of Rivers State on Saturday, MOSOP President, Fegalo Nsuke, said dialogue remains the most effective approach to resolving the protracted dispute. He called on the Federal Government to expedite the ongoing peace process to enable the Ogoni people move beyond decades of conflict and focus on development. According to Nsuke, the Ogoni struggle over the past 36 years has centred on the pursuit of justice, development, peace and environmental protection, describing the journey as costly for the people. “In a non-violent struggle, there is no better alternative to dialogue,” he said, urging Ogonis to support the ongoing engagement with the Federal Government. He noted that discussions were ongoing on a framework to address the developmental needs and demands of Ogoniland, adding that prolonging the conflict would not serve the interest of the people. Reflecting on the impact of the crisis, Nsuke said many Ogonis had suffered losses and continued to bear the scars of years of repression, but assured them that their sacrifices had not been in vain. He said the current dialogue process began on January 21, 2025, when President Bola Tinubu directed the National Security Adviser, Mallam Nuhu Ribadu, to initiate discussions with the Ogoni people through the Ogoni Dialogue Committee (ODC). According to him, the committee subsequently held consultations across Ogoniland before submitting its recommendations to the President on September 24, 2025. Nsuke described the initiative as a significant turning point in the Ogoni struggle, noting that it was the first time a Federal Government had pursued what he called an Ogoni-led dialogue process rather than attempting to resume oil exploration without addressing the concerns of the people. He commended President Tinubu for adopting a peaceful approach to the issue and also praised the National Security Adviser for his commitment to the dialogue process. “We are beginning to see positive signs of the government’s commitment to resolving the Ogoni issue in a manner that accommodates the concerns of the Ogoni people,” he said. The post Oil Resumption: Dialogue best path forward, MOSOP tells Ogonis appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Boulgou/Sécurité : Garango inaugure son commissariat de police du secteur n°3 pour renforcer la sécurité de proximité
items.description: Boulgou/Sécurité : Garango inaugure son commissariat de police du secteur n°3 pour renforcer la sécurité de proximité Garango, 1er août 2026 (AIB) – La commune de Garango, dans la province du Boulgou, région du Nakambé, a procédé, le samedi 1er août 2026, à l'inauguration du commissariat de police du secteur n°3. La cérémonie a été présidée par le Directeur général de la Police nationale, le Camarade Thierry Dofizouho Tuina, sous le patronage du Gouverneur de la région du Nakambé, le Camarade Yiyé Abraham Somdo, représenté par le Secrétaire général de la région, Tasséré Nacoulma. Elle a réuni les autorités administratives, coutumières, les forces de défense et de sécurité ainsi qu'une forte mobilisation des populations. Le Président de la délégation spéciale de la commune de Garango, les autorités locales, les responsables des forces de défense et de sécurité, les chefs coutumiers et de nombreux citoyens ont pris part à cette cérémonie, organisée sous le haut parrainage de Naaba Koom de Garango, représenté par le chef du secteur n°3. Dans son allocution, le Directeur général de la Police nationale a souligné que cette nouvelle infrastructure permettra de rapprocher davantage les services de police des populations et de renforcer le dispositif de sécurisation de la commune. Il a invité les citoyens à accompagner les forces de sécurité par une collaboration étroite afin de relever les défis sécuritaires. Les autorités locales ont, quant à elles, salué la réalisation de cet ouvrage qu'elles considèrent comme une réponse aux préoccupations des populations en matière de sécurité. Elles ont exprimé leur gratitude aux autorités nationales et à tous les acteurs ayant contribué à l'aboutissement du projet. La cérémonie a été ponctuée de prestations d'artistes locaux, de bénédictions des chefs coutumiers, d'allocutions officielles et de la remise d'un don de la population à la Police nationale en témoignage de son soutien aux missions de sécurisation. L'Office national d'identification (ONI) a également mis à profit l'événement pour procéder à l'enrôlement des citoyens en vue de l'établissement de la carte d'identité biométrique de l'Alliance des États du Sahel (AES), permettant à de nombreux habitants d'effectuer cette démarche administrative sur place. L'inauguration s'est achevée par la coupure symbolique du ruban, la visite des locaux du commissariat, une photo de famille et une séance de reboisement dans l'enceinte de l'infrastructure, marquant l'engagement des autorités à promouvoir également la protection de l'environnement. Agence D'information du Burkina BJB/SM/ata

items.title: The Law to discuss Akonta Mining and Sedina judgements
items.description: This Sunday’s edition of JoyNews’ The Law will examine two of Ghana’s most consequential court decisions in recent weeks. The Akonta Mining judgement, which saw NPP’s Bernard Antwi Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, sentenced to 20 years’ imprisonment with hard labour, and the Court of Appeal’s acquittal and discharge of former MASLOC Chief Executive Sedina Tamakloe-Attionu. The Akonta Mining case involved allegations that Wontumi and his company unlawfully assigned mineral rights and facilitated illegal mining operations without the required approvals. The Accra High Court convicted both Wontumi and Akonta Mining, a ruling that has ignited debate over the enforcement of Ghana’s mining laws, environmental protection and criminal accountability in the fight against illegal mining. The programme will also examine the Court of Appeal’s decision to acquit and discharge Sedina Tamakloe Attionu after overturning her 10-year prison sentence for causing financial loss to the state and related offences. The appellate court held that the prosecution failed to prove its case to the required legal standard and identified flaws in the trial proceedings, a decision that has fuelled discussions on prosecutorial standards, corruption prosecutions and the evidentiary threshold required for criminal convictions. Hosted by Samson Anyenini, The Law will unpack the legal reasoning behind both judgements and explore their implications for Ghana’s criminal justice system, anti-corruption efforts and the rule of law.

items.title: NDC orders completion of outstanding branch executive elections nationwide
items.description: The National Democratic Congress (NDC) has directed all its regional executives to ensure the immediate completion of outstanding Branch Executive Elections across the country, following a decision by the party’s Functional Executive Committee (FEC) aimed at finalising its grassroots electoral processes. The directive, issued by the party’s National Secretariat and signed by Deputy General Secretary (Finance and Administration), Barbara Serwaa Asamoah, on behalf of the General Secretary, instructs all Regional Chairmen and Regional Secretaries to supervise the conduct of the remaining branch elections between Monday, August 3, and Tuesday, August 11, 2026. The directive forms part of the party’s broader effort to complete outstanding internal elections and strengthen its grassroots organisational structures ahead of subsequent stages of its internal electoral calendar. According to the directive, the decision to complete all remaining Branch Executive Elections was reached during a meeting of the Functional Executive Committee held on July 28, 2026. The party explained that after reviewing the status of the internal electoral process, the FEC resolved that all outstanding branch elections should be conducted through the party’s regional structures within a specified period. “The Functional Executive Committee (FEC), at its meeting held on 28th July 2026, agreed that the outstanding Branch Executive Elections should be conducted through the Party’s various regions,” the statement said. Following that decision, regional executives have been instructed to ensure that all pending branch elections within their jurisdictions are organised and completed within the approved timeframe. “Accordingly, you are hereby directed to ensure that all outstanding Branch Executive Elections within the region are conducted from Monday, 3rd August 2026 to Tuesday, 11th August 2026,” the directive added. The nine-day exercise is expected to bring closure to all remaining branch-level electoral activities nationwide. To facilitate a smooth exercise, the National Secretariat disclosed that the list of all outstanding Branch Executive Elections has already been forwarded to the various Regional Election Committees. Regional executives have therefore been instructed to work closely with these committees throughout the electoral process to ensure effective coordination and compliance with the party’s established procedures. The directive stressed that collaboration between the regional leadership and election committees would be essential in delivering transparent, orderly and credible elections. “Please note that the list of outstanding Branch Executive Elections has already been submitted to the respective Regional Election Committees. Accordingly, you are directed to liaise closely with the Regional Election Committees to ensure that the exercise is conducted strictly in accordance with the Party’s Election Guidelines and approved timetable,” the statement said. The National Secretariat indicated that the approved timetable and election guidelines must serve as the primary framework for conducting the elections in every region. The party also directed regional officials to ensure that every aspect of the exercise complies with the NDC Constitution and all directives issued by the national leadership. According to the statement, strict compliance with the party’s constitutional provisions and electoral regulations is necessary to preserve the integrity and credibility of the internal electoral process. Regional leaders have been tasked with providing adequate supervision, logistical support and administrative oversight throughout the exercise. “This directive must be adhered to strictly to ensure the successful completion of the exercise within the stipulated period,” the communication stated. It further instructed officials to guarantee that all elections are conducted in accordance with the party’s governing rules. “You are expected to provide the necessary supervision and support to guarantee that the elections are conducted in accordance with the Party’s Constitution, Election Guidelines, and all directives issued by the Headquarters,” the directive added. The emphasis on strict adherence reflects the party’s determination to ensure that every outstanding branch election is conducted fairly, transparently and within the established legal framework. Branch Executive Elections represent one of the most important components of the NDC’s internal democratic processes, as branch executives constitute the foundation of the party’s organisational structure. Branch executives are responsible for coordinating political activities at the community level, mobilising members, implementing party programmes, recruiting new supporters and serving as the primary link between the national leadership and grassroots members. The completion of all outstanding branch elections is therefore expected to strengthen the party’s local structures by ensuring that every branch is led by duly elected executives operating under constitutional mandates. The National Secretariat appealed to regional executives to continue demonstrating commitment to the party’s organisational objectives by ensuring the successful execution of the exercise. The statement expressed confidence in the ability of regional leaders to oversee the elections professionally and within the approved schedule. “Your usual cooperation and commitment to the successful execution of this important Party assignment are highly appreciated,” the directive concluded.

items.title: At least 72 died in Spain's Ceuta migrant rush
items.description: At least 72 people died during the mass influx in recent days of migrants into Spain’s Ceuta enclave, when tens of thousands of people mostly swam around the border post from Morocco, local officials said on Sunday. Most of the estimated 60,000 people who rushed into Spain’s north African territory have returned to Morocco since the territory’s largest mass migrant crossing. “The latest figure that we have is 72,” the government’s delegate to Ceuta, Miguel Angel Perez Triano, told reporters, when asked about the number of fatalities. The previous toll was 67 deaths. Spanish police and troops patrolled the streets of Ceuta on Sunday as the enclave largely returned to normal after the sudden mass influx of migrants from Morocco that had occurred between Wednesday and Friday. Only small groups of migrants were still walking around after most who crossed the small border barrier returned voluntarily to Morocco in 48 hours. AFP on Saturday saw migrant minors milling around in a disused industrial park in Ceuta. Others were seen dozing on the pavements outside. “All the children here want to go to (mainland) Spain,” said one of the few adults at the site, Moroccan man Aziz Dabch, 41. The largest migrant rush into the enclave has caused an international crisis for Spain, with European partners criticising Madrid for its immigration policies. Outside a housing project near Ceuta port, Spanish soldiers detained a group of nine tired-looking migrants who were sitting on the pavement, guarded by troops with an armoured car, an AFP reporter said. Small inflatable boats from a rescue unit scoured the waters around the border barrier that extends into the Mediterranean Sea, where a new 500-metre (1,640-feet) floating boom reinforced security. Civil Guard were also taking migrants off a bus to escort them back to the border post to return to Morocco. The border crossing was calm, with groups of workers picking up trash, clothes and rubbish left behind during the mass crossing. Rumours Spain has blamed criminal gangs for spreading rumours that a recent Spanish Supreme Court ruling on immigration would allow migrants easier passage. Some analysts suggested Morocco could allow migrants to cross the border to put diplomatic pressure on Spain, which has recently improved ties with Rabat’s arch-enemy neighbouring Algeria. In 2021, around 10,000 migrants crossed into Ceuta, taking advantage of Morocco easing border controls as a way to pressure Spain. Moroccan officials have so far not offered any statement on the crisis. But some of those who crossed the border said they had heard the border was open — a rumour quickly amplified on social media. The EU said it would hold a video call on Tuesday after 22 bloc members issued a joint open letter calling for an urgent meeting to agree a speedy coordinated response, and to prevent further uncontrolled crossings. Italy on Saturday implemented a one-month suspension of its Schengen agreement with Spain allowing for visa-free movement between borders. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, in a letter to EU leaders, blasted the “selfish” reaction by some EU countries. Pope Leo XIV on Sunday spoke to the situation in Ceuta in his daily prayers on Sunday, saying he was following it “with concern” and hoping for a solution of “peace, stability and justice”.

items.title: Buni approves construction of four more modern markets
items.description: By Maryam Abdul-aziz Usman The Yobe State Government has approved the construction of four additional modern markets as part of efforts to expand commercial infrastructure, boost trade and strengthen economic activities across the state. The new markets will be located in Bumsa, Gulani Local Government Area; Sabon Garin Nangere in Nangere Local Government Area; Girgir in Jakusko Local Government Area; and Ngelzarma in Fune Local Government Area. The approval was contained in an official government announcement issued through the Office of the Secretary to the State Government (SSG). The statement, signed by Ibrahim Baba Saleh, Media Coordinator/Liaison in the Office of the Secretary to the State Government, said the projects would provide modern trading facilities, promote commerce in rural and urban communities, attract investment and improve the livelihoods of traders and surrounding residents. The latest approval further expands Governor Mai Mala Buni’s market infrastructure programme, one of the administration’s key strategies for stimulating economic growth, supporting small and medium-scale enterprises and strengthening post-insurgency recovery through increased commercial activities. Since assuming office in 2019, the Buni administration has completed the Damaturu, Potiskum, Nguru and Gashua ultra-modern markets, alongside modern markets in Ngalda and Yunusari. The Potiskum, Ngalda and Yunusari markets were also provided with complementary infrastructure to improve accessibility and business operations. Construction of the Geidam Ultra-Modern Market has reached over 90 per cent completion, while work is progressing on the Machina, Buni Yadi and Yusufari modern markets. With the four newly approved projects, the administration would have initiated the construction of 14 modern and ultra-modern markets across Yobe State, extending modern commercial infrastructure to more communities across the state. The government said the continued expansion of market infrastructure is expected to strengthen local economies, create employment opportunities, improve internally generated revenue, encourage private investment and provide traders with safer, more organised and efficient business environments. The initiative also aligns with the state’s broader economic diversification agenda aimed at enhancing commercial activities beyond the major urban centres and improving access to markets for rural producers and small-scale entrepreneurs. items.title: Flooding hits communities in four Yobe LGAs as SEMA begins assessment
items.description: By Maryam Abdul-aziz Usman Heavy rainfall on Saturday triggered flash floods in parts of Damaturu, Nguru, Machina and Bursari Local Government Areas of Yobe State, damaging homes and prompting emergency response by the Yobe State Emergency Management Agency (SEMA). The agency said it had received distress reports from community leaders, security agencies and local government authorities following torrential rainfall that inundated several communities. Affected communities in Damaturu include Moduri, Abbari Sabon Kwalta, Malari Sabon Kwalta, Pompomari, Sumsumma and Nayinawa. In Nguru, flooding was reported around New Side Best Centre, Balanguwa Road and communities across nine wards. Turbangini and Dinani/Lawanti Ward were affected in Bursari, while Alhaji Madi Street, Hausari and Machina town recorded incidents in Machina Local Government Area. SEMA said preliminary assessments indicate that several residential buildings sustained varying degrees of damage, while verification is ongoing to determine the number of affected households, displaced persons and possible casualties. The agency said it has deployed a multi-sectoral Rapid Assessment Team comprising SEMA officials, local government representatives and trained community volunteers to assess the impact and determine immediate humanitarian needs. The development comes days after the Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NiMet) and the Nigeria Hydrological Services Agency (NIHSA) warned of above-normal rainfall and heightened flood risk in several states, including Yobe, urging residents in flood-prone communities to relocate where necessary and observe safety precautions. The latest incident also follows concerns previously raised by residents of Nayinawa community on the outskirts of Damaturu over poor drainage infrastructure and recurring flooding, which they said exposes homes to destruction and children to drowning during the rainy season. SEMA advised residents to remain indoors during heavy rainfall, avoid floodwaters and drainage channels, disconnect electrical appliances where necessary, keep children and vulnerable persons away from flooded areas, and maintain proper hygiene to prevent water-borne diseases after flooding. The agency urged residents to cooperate with emergency responders as assessments continue, assuring that detailed findings would be released to guide relief interventions. The information was contained in Flash Incident Report No. 4 issued by the Yobe State Emergency Management Agency on August 2, 2026. items.title: Burkina/Immersion patriotique : Moumouni Zoungrana exhorte les appelés à devenir les acteurs de la transformation nationale
items.description: Burkina/Immersion patriotique : Moumouni Zoungrana exhorte les appelés à devenir les acteurs de la transformation nationale Tenkodogo, 1er août 2026 (AIB) – Le ministre de l'Enseignement secondaire, de la Formation professionnelle et technique, Dr Moumouni Zoungrana, a effectué, samedi, une visite dans deux camps d'immersion patriotique obligatoire à Tenkodogo, chef-lieu de la région du Nakambé. Il y a exhorté les nouveaux bacheliers à devenir les acteurs de la transformation nationale et du renouveau du Burkina Faso. Le ministre s'est successivement rendu à l'Institut national de formation des personnels de l'éducation (INFPE), où sont accueillies 1 096 jeunes filles, puis au collège Naaba Zoungrana, qui héberge 316 jeunes garçons. Cette visite avait pour objectif de s'enquérir des conditions de déroulement de l'immersion patriotique, d'encourager les appelés et d'échanger avec eux sur les objectifs de cette initiative. S'adressant aux nouveaux bacheliers, Dr Moumouni Zoungrana a indiqué que cette immersion vise à opérer une transformation profonde de la jeunesse burkinabè. « Nous voulons que nos enfants qui entrent dans ce camp en ressortent avec un changement dans le cœur. Qu'ils comprennent leur véritable place dans le développement et la libération du Burkina Faso », a-t-il déclaré. Selon lui, cette formation offre aux appelés l'occasion de renforcer leur esprit civique, de mieux connaître l'histoire de leur pays, ses institutions ainsi que les responsabilités qui leur incombent en tant que future élite nationale. Il les a également invités à cultiver la solidarité, à promouvoir l'unité nationale au-delà des appartenances ethniques et sociales et à préserver les valeurs culturelles burkinabè. Au cours des échanges, plusieurs appelés ont exprimé leurs préoccupations relatives à la poursuite des études après l'obtention d'un baccalauréat professionnel ou technologique. En réponse, le ministre a assuré que le Gouvernement poursuit les réformes engagées pour renforcer l'ouverture de filières adaptées dans les universités publiques, afin de permettre à tous les titulaires de ces diplômes de poursuivre leur formation. Il a précisé que, lorsque les capacités d'accueil des universités publiques sont insuffisantes, les étudiants sont orientés vers des établissements privés conventionnés, les frais de scolarité étant entièrement pris en charge par l'État. Dr Zoungrana a ajouté que des réformes sont également en cours pour élargir l'accès à l'enseignement technique et professionnel et lever certaines contraintes, notamment celles liées aux conditions d'admission. Le ministre a salué l'engagement des encadreurs, la mobilisation des autorités administratives, des Forces de défense et de sécurité, ainsi que l'accompagnement des populations, qui contribuent au bon déroulement de l'immersion patriotique. « Les informations qui nous parviennent sont satisfaisantes. En moins d'une semaine, les jeunes ont déjà acquis de nombreux enseignements. C'est une victoire que nous devons au dévouement des encadreurs », s'est-il réjoui. Avant de quitter les différents sites, Dr Moumouni Zoungrana a invité les appelés à mettre les enseignements reçus au service de leurs communautés et à devenir des ambassadeurs du patriotisme, de la discipline, de la solidarité et de la responsabilité citoyenne. Agence D'information du Burkina SM/ata
